chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When the robbing thief comes upon you, kill him. So whatever [blood/gold] he takes from you, his blood is upon my neck [as guarantee].'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.اللِّصُّ الْمُحَارِبُ: The robbing thief (one who takes wealth by force/violence)
key_terms.فَدَمُهُ فِي عُنُقِي: His blood is upon my neck (a guarantee of liability/compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing a robbing thief who attacks you according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the right of self-defense against a *muḥārib* (robber) who uses force, with Imam Ali (AS) guaranteeing the victim's blood or wealth taken as compensation. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary proof for *qatl al-muḥāir* (killing the armed robber) without requiring prior warning, emphasizing the preservation of life and property. The guarantee that 'what he took is on my neck' underscores the Imam's role as the ultimate guarantor of justice and restitution for the individual.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Bin Usman, from a man, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When a robber comes over to you, so kill him. So whatever faces you, his blood would be upon my<sup>asws</sup> neck’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Aban ibn ‘Uthaman from a man formal-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If a fighting thief enters your house, eliminate him. Whatever responsibility his blood (life) may bring is on my neck (my responsibility).”’
